Water moved in by osmosis in water and out by osmosis in salt solution

The membrane dissolved in salt solution

q: A farmer crossed two heterozygous tall plants (Tt x Tt) and got 200 offspring. A student says all short offspring got a recessive allele from both parents. What evidence proves the student right?
opts: Short plants are 25% and appear only when homozygous recessive
Tall plants are 75% because tallness is dominant
Parents were heterozygous so short plants should not appear
explain: Tt x Tt gives 1 TT:2 Tt:1 tt. Only tt shows short phenotype, so short plants must have received t from both parents.

q: Grass -> grasshopper -> frog -> snake -> hawk. A pesticide kills 90% of frogs but does not affect others directly. What is the most likely immediate effect?
opts: Snakes increase because they eat more frogs
Hawks increase due to more snakes
Grasshoppers increase, grass decreases, snakes decrease
explain: Fewer frogs means less predation on grasshoppers, so grasshoppers rise and eat more grass. Snakes lose food and decline.

q: Light peppered moths were replaced by dark moths in a soot-covered industrial area over 50 years. What best explains this change?
opts: Moths chose to become dark to hide
Soot directly changed the genes of light moths
Dark moths were better camouflaged, survived and reproduced more
Light moths migrated away because they disliked soot
explain: Variation existed. Dark form had survival advantage on soot-covered trees, so its frequency increased by natural selection.

q: A person eating only polished rice for months develops beriberi. Why does adding unpolished rice or beans prevent it?
opts: They supply thiamine (vitamin B1) needed in carbohydrate metabolism
They supply more protein to build muscle
They supply vitamin C to prevent scurvy
They supply iron to prevent anaemia
explain: Beriberi is thiamine deficiency. Polishing removes thiamine-rich bran. Unpolished rice and beans restore thiamine.

q: During a race, a runner's heart rate rises. If cardiac output = stroke volume x heart rate, why does stroke volume also rise?
opts: The heart has less time to fill so it pumps less
Blood vessels constrict to reduce flow to muscles
More venous return stretches heart muscle, causing stronger contraction
The brain stops controlling the heart
explain: Exercise increases venous return. Greater filling stretches cardiac muscle (Frank-Starling), increasing force and stroke volume.

q: A patient produces large volumes of very dilute urine. Which part is most likely failing to reabsorb water?
opts: Glomerulus, due to lack of filtration
Collecting duct, due to lack of ADH action
Proximal tubule, due to excess glucose
Loop of Henle, due to excess salt intake only
explain: ADH makes collecting duct permeable to water. Without ADH, water is not reabsorbed, producing large dilute urine.

q: A person touches a hot plate and withdraws the hand before feeling pain. Which sequence describes the reflex?
opts: Receptor -> motor neurone -> brain -> sensory neurone
Effector -> sensory neurone -> brain -> motor neurone
Receptor -> sensory neurone -> spinal cord interneurone -> motor neurone -> effector
explain: Spinal reflex bypasses brain for speed. Sensory to spinal cord, relay via interneurone, motor to muscle effector.

q: In double fertilisation, a species with 2n=14 produces a diploid zygote and triploid endosperm. What are their chromosome numbers?
explain: Zygote = egg (7) + sperm (7) = 14. Endosperm = two polar nuclei (7+7) + sperm (7) = 21.

q: Maize in waterlogged soil is stunted and yellowish despite added fertilizer. What is the most likely physiological cause?
opts: Leaves cannot photosynthesise in wet soil
Roots lack oxygen for respiration, so active uptake of ions fails
Fertilizer is washed away only by rain
explain: Waterlogged soil is anaerobic. Root cells cannot respire to make ATP for active transport, so deficiency occurs despite fertilizer.

q: Amoeba is placed in a solution that blocks ATP formation. Which function fails first?
explain: Pseudopodia formation and phagocytosis are active, ATP-dependent. Diffusion is passive and continues without ATP.

q: A couple with blood groups AB x O have children. A student says they cannot have an O child. Is the student correct?
opts: Yes, because AB parent has no i allele to give
No, because O is dominant over AB
No, because AB can produce O gametes

q: A student counted 40 grass plants in 10 quadrats of 1m2 each in a 100m2 field. What is the estimated population and main source of error?
opts: 400 plants; clumped distribution makes sampling inaccurate if not random
explain: Density = 40/10 = 4 per m2. Total = 4 x 100 = 400. Non-random / clumped distribution causes sampling bias.

q: Similar trilobite fossils are found in Africa and South America. What conclusion is best supported?
opts: Trilobites swam across the Atlantic recently
The continents were once joined, allowing similar organisms to live in both areas
Similar rocks always contain similar fossils by chance
explain: Identical fossil assemblages on now-separated continents support continental drift / common origin.

q: A child on a low-protein diet develops kwashiorkor with oedema. Why does low protein cause oedema?
opts: Low plasma protein reduces osmotic pressure, so fluid leaks into tissues
Low protein causes excess water intake
explain: Plasma proteins hold water in blood by colloid osmotic pressure. Low protein lowers it, fluid moves to tissues.

q: Xylem is blocked by an air bubble. Why does water still rise in a short plant but not a tall tree?
opts: Cohesion-tension needs a continuous column; root pressure can push only a short distance
Root pressure is the main force in tall trees
explain: Cohesion-tension requires continuous water column. Air bubble breaks it. Root pressure is weak and only effective over short distances.

q: A diabetic excretes glucose in urine despite high blood glucose. Which process has reached its limit?
opts: Secretion in distal tubule is blocked
Reabsorption in proximal tubule has reached transport maximum
Reabsorption in collecting duct is excessive
explain: Proximal tubule reabsorbs glucose by active transport with a maximum. Above renal threshold, excess remains in urine.

q: A person sees near objects well but not distant objects. Which defect and correction apply?
opts: Myopia; concave lens to diverge light onto retina
explain: Myopia: image forms in front of retina. Concave lens diverges rays to focus on retina.

q: A gardener removes the terminal bud and lateral buds grow rapidly. Which hormone interaction explains this?
opts: Removal of auxin removes apical dominance, allowing cytokinins to promote lateral growth
Removal of auxin increases gibberellin inhibition
Cytokinin from terminal bud was inhibiting laterals
Auxin from laterals was causing dormancy
explain: Terminal bud produces auxin which inhibits laterals. Removing it removes inhibition, cytokinins promote branching.

q: A mushroom is not a plant. Which characteristic best supports classifying fungi separately?
opts: Fungal walls are chitin and they are heterotrophic without chlorophyll
explain: Fungi lack chlorophyll, are heterotrophic, and have chitin walls, unlike cellulose-walled autotrophic plants.

q: In sickle cell anaemia, one base change swaps glutamic acid for valine in haemoglobin. Why does this cause severe symptoms?
opts: It changes DNA to RNA only
One amino acid cannot affect protein function
It changes haemoglobin shape, causing cells to sickle, block vessels and break down
explain: Valine is hydrophobic, causing deoxygenated HbS to polymerise, distorting cells into sickles that block capillaries.

q: A lake gets fertilizer runoff, algae bloom, then fish die. What sequence best explains fish death?
opts: Eutrophication -> bloom -> decomposition uses oxygen -> oxygen depletion kills fish
explain: Nutrient enrichment causes bloom. Dead algae decomposed by bacteria consume dissolved oxygen, creating hypoxia.

q: Human, bat and whale forelimbs have the same bone pattern but different functions. What does this provide evidence for?
opts: Divergent evolution from a common ancestor
explain: Homologous structures with same basic plan but different functions indicate divergent evolution from a common ancestor.

q: A baby gets antibodies from breast milk. What type of immunity is this and why does it not last?
opts: Natural active immunity; baby makes antibodies
Natural passive immunity; antibodies are not made by baby and break down
Artificial active immunity; baby is immunised
explain: Mother's antibodies give passive immunity. Baby makes no memory cells, so protection is temporary.

q: A leafy shoot in a potometer absorbs water faster in bright light and wind than in dim still air. What is the direct cause?
opts: Light directly pushes water into leaf
Increased transpiration creates stronger pull, increasing uptake
explain: Light opens stomata and wind removes humid air, both increase transpiration, increasing pull and uptake.

q: Soil pH is 3.5. Crops fail despite fertilizer. What is the most appropriate intervention and why?
opts: Add lime to raise pH, because extreme acidity locks up nutrients and damages roots
explain: Very acidic soil makes phosphorus unavailable and aluminium toxic. Liming raises pH, improving nutrient availability.

q: Why does a nerve impulse travel faster in a myelinated neurone than unmyelinated?
opts: Myelin slows impulse to save energy
Nodes generate impulse continuously along whole axon
Myelin insulates and impulse jumps between nodes by saltatory conduction
explain: Myelin prevents ion leakage. Depolarisation jumps from node to node, much faster than continuous conduction.

q: A woman with a 28-day cycle ovulates around day 14. If fertilisation occurs, which hormone maintains the corpus luteum?
opts: Follicle stimulating hormone from the ovary
Human chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) from the embryo
Oxytocin from the pituitary only after birth
explain: Implanting embryo secretes hCG which sustains corpus luteum to continue progesterone, maintaining pregnancy.

q: In a dicot stem bundles form a ring, in monocot they are scattered. What does this imply for secondary growth?
opts: Dicot can undergo secondary growth from vascular cambium; monocot generally cannot
Arrangement has no effect on growth
explain: Dicot ring allows cambium to form continuous ring. Scattered monocot bundles lack organised cambium.

q: Bacteria divide every 20 minutes. Starting from 1 cell, how many after 2 hours if no death, and why is this unrealistic in nature?
opts: 64 cells; nutrients deplete and waste accumulates, limiting growth
64 cells; growth continues forever in nature
explain: 2 hours = 6 generations. 2^6 = 64. In nature, limiting factors prevent unlimited exponential growth.

q: A green plant kept in darkness for 48 hours then tested for starch gives a negative result. What conclusion is valid?
opts: Plant died and cannot make starch
Plant used starch to make chlorophyll
Starch was used up in respiration and no photosynthesis occurred to replace it
explain: In darkness, no photosynthesis, but respiration continues, using up starch reserves.

q: Children of a tall man and short woman show varied heights. Which genetic pattern best explains continuous variation in height?
explain: Height is controlled by many genes plus nutrition/environment, producing continuous range.

q: In an aquatic system, the pyramid of biomass can be inverted. Why?
opts: Producers are eaten by decomposers only
Phytoplankton reproduce rapidly and are eaten quickly, so standing biomass is small despite high productivity
explain: Pyramid of biomass measures standing crop. Fast turnover of phytoplankton means small standing biomass but high production.

q: Bat wings and insect wings are both used for flight but have different structures. What term describes this?
explain: Different origin, same function = analogous. They evolved independently for flight.

q: A person with goitre has an enlarged thyroid from iodine deficiency. Why does lack of iodine cause enlargement?
opts: Iodine directly causes thyroid to shrink
Goitre is caused by excess iodine only
Low thyroxine leads to increased TSH, which stimulates thyroid growth
explain: Iodine needed for thyroxine. Low thyroxine removes feedback, pituitary secretes more TSH, overstimulating thyroid.

q: A root grows downward and shoot grows upward. Which hormone distribution explains root bending?
opts: Auxin accumulates on upper side and promotes growth
Auxin accumulates on lower side of root and inhibits growth there, causing downward bending
explain: In roots, high auxin inhibits elongation. Gravity causes auxin to accumulate lower side, that side grows slower, root bends down.

q: A dialysis machine is used for kidney failure. Which kidney function does it replace?
opts: Production of urine by the bladder
Removal of urea and excess salts and water by diffusion across semi-permeable membrane
Production of red blood cells only
explain: Dialysis uses diffusion across membrane to remove waste and balance salts/water, mimicking filtration/reabsorption.

q: If fertilisation does not occur, the corpus luteum degenerates. What happens next?
opts: Oestrogen rises and ovulation occurs immediately
Progesterone falls, endometrium breaks down and menstruation occurs
Progesterone rises and pregnancy is maintained
explain: Without hCG, corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone drops, lining cannot be maintained, it sheds.

q: A seed has large endosperm and small embryo. During germination, endosperm shrinks. What is the role of gibberellins?
opts: Gibberellins trigger aleurone to produce amylase, which digests endosperm starch for embryo
explain: Embryo releases gibberellins, stimulating aleurone to secrete amylase, hydrolysing stored starch to sugars.

q: A virus is not considered living. Which evidence best supports this?
opts: It cannot reproduce or carry out metabolism outside a host cell
explain: Viruses lack cellular machinery, cannot generate energy or reproduce independently, requiring host cell.

q: Yeast + glucose in two tubes, one with air, one sealed. Sealed tube produces less energy but bubbles. Why?
opts: Anaerobic produces ethanol + CO2 and only 2 ATP per glucose, versus aerobic produces CO2 + water and 38 ATP
explain: Anaerobic incompletely breaks glucose, yielding little ATP and ethanol + CO2. Aerobic yields full ATP.

q: If all decomposers were removed from an ecosystem, what would happen first?
opts: Nutrient cycling stops, dead matter accumulates, producers run out of minerals
explain: Decomposers mineralise dead matter, returning nutrients to soil. Without them, nutrients lock up.

100%, because father passes X to sons
explain: Woman's father XcY gives Xc to daughter, so mother is carrier. Sons: 50% get Xc = colour-blind.

q: A plant in a dry habitat has sunken stomata and thick cuticle. What is the main advantage?
opts: Reduces transpiration water loss while still allowing gas exchange when needed
explain: Sunken stomata trap humid air, reducing diffusion gradient. Thick cuticle reduces cuticular transpiration.

q: During muscle contraction, calcium ions are released from sarcoplasmic reticulum. What is their role?
opts: They bind to troponin, exposing binding sites for myosin on actin
explain: Ca2+ binds troponin, moving tropomyosin, exposing actin sites. Myosin cross-bridges then form.

q: A leaf has many more stomata on lower surface than upper. Why is this adaptive?
opts: Reduces water loss from upper surface exposed to sun while allowing gas exchange below
explain: Upper surface receives direct sun and heat, more stomata there would increase transpiration. Lower is cooler.

q: In a food chain, DDT accumulates more in top predators than in producers. What process is this?
opts: Biomagnification, because DDT is not broken down and concentrates at each trophic level
explain: Persistent DDT is taken up and not excreted, concentration increases up the chain.

q: A woman with blood group O has a baby with blood group AB. A man with blood group O claims he is the father. Can he be?

No, O x O can only produce O children, AB requires A and B alleles

q: A leaf disc floats in sodium bicarbonate solution under light but sinks in darkness. Why?
opts: Photosynthesis in light produces oxygen bubbles that lift disc; in darkness respiration consumes oxygen
explain: Bicarbonate provides CO2. Oxygen produced accumulates, increasing buoyancy. In darkness, no O2 produced.

q: Bacteria exposed to antibiotics: a few survive and multiply. After repeated exposure, most are resistant. This is an example of?

explain: Variation for resistance existed before. Antibiotic selects resistant variants, they survive and reproduce.

q: A student sets up two identical seedlings, one in a pot with soil and one with roots in water containing mineral salts. After 2 weeks the soil plant grows better. What is the best explanation?

Roots cannot absorb minerals from water
explain: Water culture can lack oxygen around roots and cause poor aeration. Soil gives air spaces, water retention and minerals in correct balance.

q: A red blood cell is placed in a solution and no change in size occurs. What can be concluded about the solution?
opts: It is isotonic to the cell
explain: No net movement means water potential inside equals outside, so solution is isotonic.

q: In an experiment, a leaf is covered with black paper on one side and left in light. After starch test, only the uncovered part turns blue-black. What does this prove?
opts: Light is not needed for starch formation
Chlorophyll is in the black paper
Starch is made only in darkness
Light is necessary for photosynthesis and starch formation
explain: Only the illuminated part photosynthesised and made starch. Covered part had no light so no starch.

q: A couple are both carriers for sickle cell (AS x AS). What is the chance their first child has sickle cell anaemia (SS)?
explain: AS x AS gives 1 AA : 2 AS : 1 SS. Chance of SS is 1 in 4 = 25%.

q: A fish is taken from fresh water and put in sea water. It dies. Why?
opts: It gains too much water by osmosis
It loses water by osmosis and cannot replace it fast enough
It cannot breathe in sea water
explain: Sea water is hypertonic to freshwater fish. Water leaves body by osmosis, fish dehydrates.

q: A plant with variegated leaves has green and white patches. The white patch tested negative for starch after light. What does this show?

explain: White patches lack chlorophyll, so no photosynthesis and no starch, even in light.

q: Why does cutting a shoot and placing it in water cause it to wilt less if leaves are removed?
opts: Fewer leaves means less transpiration and water loss
explain: Leaves are main site of transpiration. Removing them reduces water loss while roots are absent.

q: A person with blood group A receives blood from a donor with blood group B. What happens?

explain: Group A has anti-B antibodies. They attack B antigens on donor cells, causing agglutination.

q: In a food web, removing all hawks causes snakes to increase then decrease. Why the decrease?
opts: Snakes overeat frogs, frogs fall, then snakes starve
explain: Without predators snakes rise, overeat prey, prey crashes, then snakes starve due to lack of food.

q: A student breathes into limewater and it turns milky faster after exercise than at rest. Why?
opts: More CO2 is exhaled after exercise due to increased respiration
explain: Exercise increases respiration to release more energy, producing more CO2 which turns limewater milky.

q: A DNA sample has 30% adenine. What percentage is cytosine?
explain: A = T = 30%, so A+T = 60%. Remaining 40% is G+C, so G = C = 20%.

q: A plant is kept in a sealed bell jar with a mouse. Both survive longer than alone. What explains this?
opts: Plant produces oxygen for mouse, mouse produces CO2 for plant
explain: Photosynthesis uses CO2 and releases O2. Respiration uses O2 and releases CO2. They balance each other.

q: Why does a person feel thirsty after eating salty food?
opts: Salt increases blood water potential, stimulating thirst centre
explain: Salty food raises blood osmotic pressure. Osmoreceptors stimulate thirst to restore water balance.

q: A farmer sprays insecticide that kills pollinators. Next season fruit yield falls drastically. What is the direct link?
opts: Pollinators are needed for pollination and fertilisation to form fruit
explain: Without pollinators, pollen transfer fails, fertilisation does not occur, so fruit does not form.

q: A tadpole in a pond with low iodine develops but does not metamorphose into a frog. Why?
opts: Iodine is needed for thyroxine which controls metamorphosis
explain: Thyroxine requires iodine. Without it, metamorphosis is blocked.

q: Two plants of same species grow, one in shade and one in sun. The shade plant has larger, thinner leaves. Why is this adaptive?
opts: To increase surface area to capture scarce light
explain: Large thin leaves maximise light capture in low light for photosynthesis.

q: A person with diabetes insipidus produces large urine volume. A doctor gives ADH. Urine volume falls. What does this prove?
opts: ADH increases water reabsorption in collecting duct
Diabetes insipidus is caused by excess ADH
explain: ADH makes collecting duct permeable to water, increasing reabsorption and reducing urine volume.

q: In a cross, all F1 are tall. F1 selfed gives 3 tall : 1 short. What were the parental genotypes?
explain: TT x tt gives all Tt tall in F1. F1 Tt x Tt gives 3:1 ratio.

q: Why does a cut stem placed in eosin dye show dye only in xylem after some time?
opts: Xylem is the only tissue that transports water up
Xylem is dead so dye fills it
explain: Xylem carries water and dissolved substances upward from roots. Dye follows transpiration stream in xylem.

q: A child eats a meal high in starch but no protein for weeks. What deficiency is most likely?
explain: Starch provides energy but no protein. Lack of protein causes kwashiorkor.

q: A muscle is stimulated repeatedly without rest and stops contracting. What is this called and why?
opts: Tetanus due to lack of ATP and accumulation of waste
Fatigue due to too much ATP
explain: Repeated contraction uses ATP and builds lactic acid. ATP depletion prevents cross-bridge cycling, causing fatigue.

q: A leaf is boiled in water, then in alcohol, then tested with iodine. Why boil in alcohol?
opts: To remove chlorophyll so iodine colour shows
explain: Alcohol removes chlorophyll which would mask the blue-black iodine result.

q: In an ecosystem, the number of producers is always greater than herbivores. Why?
opts: Energy is lost at each transfer, so fewer consumers can be supported
explain: Only about 10% energy transfers. Producers must be abundant to support fewer herbivores.

q: A woman has a 28-day cycle. On day 14, LH surges. What is the immediate effect?
explain: LH surge causes rupture of Graafian follicle and release of egg, ovulation.

q: A seed is planted deep in soil and does not germinate. What is the most likely reason?
opts: Lack of oxygen and low temperature at depth, and plumule cannot reach light
explain: Deep soil has less oxygen and light. Seedling cannot reach surface before food reserves run out.

q: Why does blood clot faster when exposed to air?
opts: Damaged tissue and air trigger platelet release and clotting cascade
explain: Exposure activates platelets and clotting factors, forming fibrin mesh to seal wound.

q: A student places a potted plant in a dark cupboard for 3 days. Its leaves turn yellow. Why?
opts: Chlorophyll breaks down without light and is not replaced
explain: Chlorophyll needs light for synthesis. In darkness it degrades and is not replaced, revealing yellow pigments.

q: A person eats a lot of carbohydrate but does little exercise and gains weight. Why?
opts: Carbohydrate is stored as fat when in excess
Exercise is needed to digest carbohydrate
explain: Excess glucose is converted to glycogen then fat for storage, increasing body mass.

q: In the kidney, glucose is found in glomerular filtrate but not in urine of a healthy person. Why?
opts: Glucose is reabsorbed in proximal tubule
explain: All glucose is filtered, then fully reabsorbed by active transport in proximal tubule in healthy person.

q: A plant with closed stomata on a hot day wilts less but photosynthesises less. What is the trade-off?
opts: Closing stomata saves water but reduces CO2 entry for photosynthesis
explain: Stomata control both water loss and gas exchange. Closing saves water but limits CO2.

q: Why are xerophytes able to survive in deserts?
opts: They store water and reduce transpiration
explain: Thick cuticle, reduced leaves, water storage and sunken stomata reduce water loss and store water.

q: A baby is born with blood group O to a mother with blood group A. The father claims he is group AB. Is this possible?
opts: Yes, A x AB can produce O
No, AB parent cannot give i allele, so O child impossible
No, mother is A so child must be A
explain: O child is ii, needs i from both parents. AB parent has no i allele, so cannot have O child.

q: A person with anaemia feels tired and breathless. Why?
opts: Less haemoglobin means less oxygen carried to tissues for respiration
explain: Low haemoglobin reduces oxygen delivery, so less aerobic respiration and less energy.

q: In a population, dark moths increased after pollution. What would happen if pollution is cleaned?
opts: Dark moths would continue to increase
Light moths would increase again because they are better camouflaged on clean trees
explain: Selection reverses. Light form becomes better camouflaged on clean bark, survives more.

q: Why does a nerve impulse not travel backwards along a neurone?
explain: Neurotransmitter is released only from presynaptic side, receptor only on postsynaptic side, so impulse is one-way at synapse.

q: A student observes that a cactus has spines not leaves. What is the function of spines?
opts: To reduce transpiration and deter herbivores
explain: Spines are modified leaves with small surface area, reducing water loss and protecting plant.

q: A person with a diet low in vitamin D develops rickets. Why does vitamin D deficiency cause soft bones?
opts: Vitamin D is needed for calcium absorption, without it bones lack calcium
Rickets is caused by excess calcium
explain: Vitamin D promotes calcium absorption in gut. Low vitamin D means low calcium for bone mineralisation.

q: In a test cross, a tall plant crossed with a short plant gives all tall offspring. What is the tall plant genotype?
explain: Test cross with tt: if parent is TT, all offspring Tt tall. If Tt, 1:1 tall:short would appear.

q: A plant root grows towards water. What is this response called?
explain: Growth towards water is hydrotropism, a positive tropism.

q: Why does the heart have valves?
explain: Valves ensure one-way flow, preventing backflow when chambers relax.

q: A student puts a drop of blood on a slide and adds anti-A serum. Clumping occurs. What is the blood group?
explain: Clumping with anti-A means A antigen present, so group A (or AB if also clumps with anti-B). With only anti-A result, group A.

q: A lake has many fish but few algae. After adding phosphate, algae bloom and fish die. What is the primary cause of fish death?
opts: Oxygen depletion from decomposition of dead algae
explain: Algal bloom dies, bacteria decompose it using oxygen, causing hypoxia and fish death.

q: A person touches a cold object and withdraws hand. Which is the effector?
explain: Effector carries out response. Muscle contracts to withdraw hand.

q: Why do desert animals produce very concentrated urine?
explain: Concentrated urine means less water lost, conserving water in dry environment.

q: In photosynthesis, oxygen comes from which molecule?
explain: Photolysis splits water, releasing oxygen. CO2 provides carbon for glucose.

q: A plant is heterozygous for seed colour (Yy). What gametes does it produce?
opts: Y and y in equal ratio
explain: Meiosis separates alleles, so half gametes get Y, half get y.

q: Why does a person with high blood pressure have increased risk of stroke?
opts: High pressure can damage blood vessels in brain
High pressure has no effect on brain
explain: High pressure stresses vessel walls, can cause rupture or blockage in brain.

q: A student counts bubbles from pondweed in light and dark. More bubbles in light. What do bubbles show?
opts: Rate of photosynthesis as oxygen is released
explain: Bubbles are oxygen from photosynthesis. More bubbles = faster photosynthesis.

q: A couple with normal vision have a colour-blind son. What is the mother's genotype?
explain: Son gets Xc from mother. Mother is phenotypically normal so must be carrier XCXc.

q: In a dicot leaf, palisade mesophyll is near upper surface. Why?
opts: To receive maximum light for photosynthesis
explain: Palisade cells have many chloroplasts and are positioned to capture light.

q: A student places a wilted plant in water and it becomes turgid in 2 hours. A second wilted plant in concentrated sugar solution stays wilted. What explains the difference?
opts: Water enters by osmosis in water but leaves by osmosis in sugar solution
Sugar enters the plant and poisons it
Water is absorbed by active transport only in sugar
The plant photosynthesises faster in sugar
explain: Water moves from high to low water potential. Pure water enters cells, sugar solution draws water out.

q: A man with blood group AB marries a woman with blood group O. A child is born with blood group A. A student claims the child cannot be theirs. Is the student right?
opts: Yes, AB x O cannot produce A
No, AB x O can produce A and B children
explain: AB parent gives IA or IB. O parent gives i. IAi = group A, IBi = group B. A child is possible.

q: In a pond, algae increase rapidly, then zooplankton increase, then both crash. What best explains the crash?
opts: Zooplankton eat all algae then starve, algae then lack nutrients
explain: Zooplankton overgraze algae, algae crash, then zooplankton starve. Predator-prey oscillation.

q: A patient is given a drug that blocks acetylcholinesterase. What happens at the neuromuscular junction?
explain: Acetylcholinesterase breaks down acetylcholine. Blocking it leaves acetylcholine in synapse, continuous stimulation.

q: A cross between red-flowered (RR) and white-flowered (rr) snapdragons gives pink F1. F1 selfed gives 1 red:2 pink:1 white. What inheritance is this?
explain: Heterozygote shows intermediate phenotype, pink, not red. 1:2:1 ratio shows incomplete dominance.

q: A leaf is kept in light with CO2-free air. Starch test is negative. What does this prove?
explain: Without CO2, no carbon fixation, no glucose/starch, even with light.

q: Why does a person with a blocked bile duct have pale faeces and poor fat digestion?
opts: Bile contains enzymes that digest fat
Bile emulsifies fat and gives faeces colour from bile pigments
explain: Bile emulsifies fat for lipase and contains bilirubin pigment that colours faeces. Blockage removes both.

q: A seed is soaked and the embryo is removed. The endosperm does not digest starch. What does this show?
opts: Embryo produces gibberellin needed to trigger amylase
explain: Embryo releases gibberellins that trigger aleurone to make amylase. Without embryo, no signal.

q: In a closed ecosystem, all decomposers die. What happens to carbon cycle first?
opts: Dead matter accumulates and CO2 release falls
explain: Decomposers release CO2 by respiration. Without them, carbon stays locked in dead matter.

q: A woman is Rh-negative and carries an Rh-positive baby. After first birth she is given anti-D. Why?
opts: To prevent her making anti-D antibodies that would attack next Rh-positive baby
explain: Anti-D destroys fetal Rh-positive cells in mother before she makes her own antibodies, preventing haemolytic disease.

q: A plant in a potometer shows faster water uptake in wind than still air. Why does wind increase uptake?
opts: Wind removes humid air around leaf, increasing transpiration pull
explain: Wind removes saturated air layer, maintains steep diffusion gradient, increases transpiration and pull.

q: A DNA molecule has 200 bases. 60 are guanine. How many thymine bases are there?
explain: G=C=60, so G+C=120. Remaining 80 are A+T, so A=T=40.

q: A student measures oxygen uptake of germinating seeds at 20C and 30C. Uptake is higher at 30C. Why?
opts: Enzymes work faster up to optimum, increasing respiration
Oxygen dissolves better at high temp
explain: Respiration is enzyme-controlled. Higher temperature increases enzyme activity and respiration rate.

q: A person with kidney failure has high urea in blood. Why does dialysis reduce it?
opts: Urea diffuses from blood to dialysis fluid down concentration gradient
explain: Dialysis membrane allows urea to diffuse from high in blood to low in fluid, removing waste.

q: A population of beetles has green and brown forms. Birds eat green more on brown soil. After 10 generations brown increases. What is this?
explain: Brown beetles are better camouflaged, survive predation, reproduce more. Selection changes frequency.

q: Why does a nerve impulse travel one way across a synapse?
opts: Neurotransmitter is released only from presynaptic membrane and receptors only on postsynaptic
explain: Synaptic vesicles are only in presynaptic terminal, receptors only on postsynaptic membrane, so one-way.

q: A plant with variegated leaves is destarched, then kept in light. Only green parts test positive for starch. What is proven?
opts: Starch is made in white parts
explain: White parts lack chlorophyll, cannot photosynthesise, no starch. Green parts with chlorophyll make starch.

q: A man is colour-blind. His wife is normal with no family history. What is chance their daughter is colour-blind?
explain: Daughter gets Xc from father and XC from mother, so XCXc carrier, not colour-blind. 0% affected.

q: A fish in fresh water drinks very little water and produces large dilute urine. Why?
opts: Water enters by osmosis, so it must excrete excess water and conserve salts
explain: Fresh water is hypotonic, water enters by osmosis. Fish excretes excess water, reabsorbs salts.

q: In a food chain, energy transfer is about 10%. If producers have 10000 kJ, how much reaches tertiary consumer?
explain: Primary gets 1000, secondary 100, tertiary 10 kJ. 10% each level.

q: A student cuts a stem and puts it in water. Air bubbles enter xylem and water stops rising. Why?
opts: Air breaks continuous water column needed for cohesion-tension
explain: Cohesion-tension needs continuous column. Air bubble breaks it, pull fails.

q: A person eats only meat for months and develops constipation. Why?
opts: Meat has no fibre, so faeces move slowly and more water is absorbed
explain: Fibre adds bulk and retains water. Without fibre, faeces are dry, slow, constipation.

q: A couple both have genotype Aa for albinism. What is chance of a normal child who is a carrier?
explain: Aa x Aa gives 1 AA:2 Aa:1 aa. Carrier normal = Aa = 50%.

q: Why does a plant kept in a sealed jar with soda lime die?
opts: Soda lime absorbs CO2, so photosynthesis stops
explain: Soda lime absorbs CO2. Without CO2, photosynthesis cannot occur, plant starves.

q: A child with kwashiorkor has swollen belly and thin limbs. What is the main cause?
opts: Protein deficiency causing low plasma proteins and fluid leakage
explain: Low protein reduces plasma osmotic pressure, fluid leaks to tissues, oedema and swollen belly.

q: In the eye, light is focused by cornea and lens onto retina. A person cannot see distant objects. Where does image form?
explain: In myopia eyeball is too long, image forms in front of retina.

q: A student adds yeast to glucose solution and seals tube. After an hour tube smells of alcohol. Why?
opts: Yeast respires anaerobically, producing ethanol and CO2
explain: Without oxygen, yeast carries out anaerobic respiration, ethanol + CO2, alcohol smell.

q: A lake is polluted with sewage. Bacterial population rises, then fish die. Why do fish die?
opts: Bacteria use up oxygen during decomposition
explain: Bacteria decompose sewage, consume dissolved oxygen, fish suffocate from hypoxia.

q: A plant is exposed to unilateral light and bends towards light. Where is auxin highest?
explain: Auxin moves to shaded side, promotes faster elongation there, bending towards light.

q: A person with diabetes has glucose in urine. Why does this happen?
opts: Blood glucose exceeds renal threshold, proximal tubule cannot reabsorb all
explain: High blood glucose exceeds transport maximum for reabsorption, excess stays in urine.

q: In a population, allele for sickle cell persists despite causing disease. Why?
opts: Heterozygotes are resistant to malaria, so have advantage
explain: AS heterozygotes resist malaria, so allele is maintained by balancing selection.

q: A leaf disc in bicarbonate solution floats faster in bright light than dim light. Why?
opts: Photosynthesis produces oxygen faster in bright light
explain: More light increases photosynthesis rate, more O2 bubbles, disc floats faster.

q: Why does blood pressure rise during exercise?
opts: Heart rate and cardiac output increase to supply muscles
Blood vessels dilate in all tissues
explain: Exercise increases heart rate and stroke volume, cardiac output rises, pressure rises.

q: A student observes that a frog's webbed feet help swimming. What type of adaptation is this?
explain: Webbed feet are a physical structure for swimming, structural adaptation.

q: A plant is watered with salt water and wilts. Why does it not recover when watered with fresh water later?
opts: Salt damages root cells by plasmolysis and ion toxicity
explain: Salt causes water loss and ion toxicity, damaging membranes and root cells irreversibly.

q: A man has blood group O and woman has blood group AB. What blood groups can their children have?
explain: O is ii, AB is IAIB. Children get IAi = A, IBi = B. Only A and B.

q: In a nerve cell, sodium ions rush in during depolarisation. What causes this?
opts: Sodium channels open, sodium moves down concentration gradient
explain: Stimulus opens voltage-gated Na+ channels, Na+ rushes in down gradient, depolarising membrane.

q: A student places a fresh leaf in boiling water then alcohol then iodine. It turns blue-black. What was the purpose of boiling in water?
opts: To kill cells and break membranes so alcohol can enter
explain: Boiling kills cells, denatures enzymes, breaks membranes, allowing chlorophyll extraction.

q: Why do farmers rotate crops with legumes?
opts: Legumes fix nitrogen, restoring soil fertility
explain: Legumes have Rhizobium that fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching soil for next crop.

q: A person with a goitre has low thyroxine. Why does pituitary secrete more TSH?
opts: Negative feedback is lost, so TSH rises
explain: Low thyroxine removes negative feedback, pituitary releases more TSH to stimulate thyroid.

q: In an experiment, two identical plants, one with Vaseline on upper leaf surface, one on lower. Lower Vaseline plant wilts less. Why?
opts: Most stomata are on lower surface, blocking them reduces transpiration
explain: Most stomata are lower. Blocking them greatly reduces water loss.

q: A child is born with extra chromosome 21. What is this condition and cause?
explain: Trisomy 21 from non-disjunction, homologous chromosomes fail to separate, gamete gets extra 21.

q: Why does a person feel dizzy after standing quickly?
opts: Blood pools in legs, brain gets less blood briefly
explain: Gravity pulls blood to legs, venous return and brain blood flow drop briefly, dizziness.

q: A plant is kept in darkness and its starch is used up. If then kept in light with CO2, starch returns. What does this show?
opts: Starch is made only in darkness
Photosynthesis makes starch using light and CO2
explain: Light + CO2 allow photosynthesis to produce glucose, stored as starch.

q: In a food web, if all herbivores are removed, what happens to producers?
opts: Producers increase initially, then competition and disease may limit
explain: Without grazing, producers grow unchecked initially, then competition for light/nutrients limits.

q: A student puts a drop of blood in distilled water and observes cells burst. What is this called?
explain: Water enters by osmosis, cell swells and bursts, haemolysis.

q: Why does a muscle need oxygen during sustained exercise?
opts: To produce ATP aerobically for contraction
explain: Aerobic respiration uses oxygen to produce large ATP for sustained contraction.

q: A couple with normal vision have a colour-blind daughter. What must be true?
opts: Father is colour-blind and mother is carrier
explain: Daughter needs Xc from both parents. Father must be XcY, mother must be at least carrier.

q: A plant root is placed in a solution with high auxin. Root growth is inhibited. Why?
opts: High auxin inhibits root elongation but promotes shoot elongation
explain: Roots are sensitive to auxin. Low promotes, high inhibits elongation.

q: In the kidney, what happens in the loop of Henle?
opts: Water reabsorption and salt concentration in medulla
explain: Loop creates medullary gradient, water leaves descending limb, salt leaves ascending, concentrating urine.

q: A student crosses a black mouse (BB) with white mouse (bb). All F1 are black. What is F1 genotype?
explain: Black is dominant. BB x bb gives all Bb, black phenotype.

q: Why does a person with anaemia have pale skin?
opts: Less haemoglobin means less red colour
explain: Low haemoglobin reduces red colour of blood, skin appears pale.

q: A forest is cut down and replaced with farmland. What happens to carbon dioxide levels?
opts: CO2 rises because fewer trees photosynthesise and burning releases CO2
explain: Fewer trees mean less CO2 uptake, plus decomposition/burning releases CO2.

q: A student observes that a cactus has a thick cuticle. What is its function?
explain: Thick waxy cuticle reduces cuticular transpiration, conserving water.

q: In a synapse, calcium ions enter presynaptic terminal. What do they do?
opts: They trigger release of neurotransmitter vesicles
explain: Ca2+ influx causes vesicles to fuse with membrane, releasing neurotransmitter.

q: A plant is grown in a solution lacking magnesium. Leaves turn yellow between veins. Why?
opts: Magnesium is needed for chlorophyll, deficiency causes chlorosis
Magnesium is needed for cell wall
explain: Mg is central atom of chlorophyll. Without it, chlorophyll cannot form, leaves yellow.

q: A person eats a meal and blood glucose rises. Insulin is released. What does insulin do?
opts: Promotes uptake of glucose and conversion to glycogen in liver/muscle
explain: Insulin lowers blood glucose by increasing uptake and glycogenesis.

q: In a population, light and dark moths coexist. What maintains both?
explain: Different backgrounds favour different forms at different times, maintaining polymorphism.

q: Why does a leaf kept in a sealed bag with KOH not produce starch?
explain: KOH absorbs CO2, removing raw material for photosynthesis.

q: A student places a snail in a jar with a plant in light. Both survive. In dark, snail dies first. Why?
opts: Plant in dark respires and uses oxygen, competing with snail
explain: In dark, plant cannot photosynthesise, both respire and compete for oxygen, oxygen runs out.

q: A woman with blood group A has a child with blood group O. The father is blood group B. What are parental genotypes?
explain: O child needs i from both. Mother must be AO, father BO.

q: Why does a person with a fever have increased metabolic rate?
opts: Enzymes work faster at higher temp, increasing respiration
explain: Higher temperature increases enzyme activity and metabolic rate up to a point.

q: In a dicot stem, vascular cambium produces secondary xylem and phloem. What is the result?
explain: Secondary growth adds layers, increasing girth.

q: A student adds Benedict's solution to a food sample and heats it. It turns brick-red. What is present?
explain: Benedict's tests for reducing sugars, brick-red indicates high amount.

q: Why does a person with blocked coronary artery have chest pain?
opts: Heart muscle lacks oxygen for respiration
Heart muscle gets too much oxygen
explain: Blocked artery reduces oxygen to heart muscle, cells respire anaerobically, pain and damage.

q: A plant is bent by wind and grows thicker stem. What is this called?
explain: Mechanical stress induces thicker, shorter growth, thigmomorphogenesis.

q: In a food chain, DDT is found at higher concentration in hawk than in grass. Why?
opts: DDT is not broken down and accumulates up chain
explain: Biomagnification: persistent chemical concentrates at each trophic level.

q: A student observes that a red blood cell has no nucleus. What is the advantage?
opts: More space for haemoglobin to carry oxygen
explain: Loss of nucleus gives more room for haemoglobin and biconcave shape for oxygen transport.

q: Why does a person with diabetes insipidus drink a lot of water?
opts: Kidneys lose water due to lack of ADH, so thirst compensates
explain: No ADH means collecting duct does not reabsorb water, large urine loss, thirst to replace.

q: A plant is grown in a solution with no nitrate. It grows stunted and yellow. Why?
opts: Nitrate is needed for protein and chlorophyll synthesis
Nitrate is needed for cell wall only
Nitrate is needed for water uptake
explain: Nitrate provides nitrogen for amino acids, proteins, chlorophyll. Deficiency causes chlorosis and poor growth.

q: In a cross, a plant with genotype TtYy is selfed. What proportion is ttyy?
explain: Tt x Tt gives tt 1/4, Yy x Yy gives yy 1/4. Combined 1/4 x 1/4 = 1/16.

q: Why does a person feel hungry after insulin injection?
opts: Insulin lowers blood glucose, brain detects low glucose
explain: Insulin lowers blood glucose. Low glucose triggers hunger centre.

q: A student places a leaf in a sealed tube with a CO2 indicator. In light indicator turns purple (low CO2), in dark turns yellow (high CO2). Why?
opts: Photosynthesis uses CO2 in light, respiration releases CO2 in dark
explain: In light photosynthesis exceeds respiration, CO2 falls. In dark only respiration, CO2 rises.

q: In an ecosystem, the pyramid of numbers can be inverted. When?
opts: When one tree supports many insects
explain: One large tree (producer) can support many insects, pyramid inverted.

q: A person with a spinal cord injury cannot feel pain in legs but can move them. What is damaged?
explain: Sensory pathway damaged, so sensation lost, motor pathway intact, movement remains.

q: Why does a seed need oxygen to germinate?
opts: For aerobic respiration to release energy for growth
explain: Germination needs ATP from aerobic respiration, which needs oxygen.

q: A student observes that a flower has bright petals and nectar. What is the function?
explain: Bright petals and nectar attract insects for pollination.

q: In the heart, the left ventricle wall is thicker than right. Why?
opts: Left pumps blood to whole body, needs more force
explain: Left ventricle pumps to systemic circulation, high pressure, needs thick muscle.

q: A plant is exposed to drought and stomata close. What happens to transpiration and photosynthesis?
opts: Transpiration falls, photosynthesis falls due to less CO2
explain: Closed stomata reduce water loss but also reduce CO2 entry, limiting photosynthesis.

q: Why does a person with a high fever sweat?
In a population, a new allele appears by mutation. What determines if it spreads?
opts: Whether it gives survival advantage and is inherited
Whether it is in somatic cells
Whether it is caused by environment
explain: Only germline mutations are inherited. Advantage increases frequency by selection.

q: A student puts a piece of potato in concentrated salt solution and it shrinks. What process is this?
explain: Water leaves potato cells by osmosis to hypertonic solution, cells become plasmolysed.

q: Why does a person with liver disease have low plasma protein?
opts: Liver makes plasma proteins, damaged liver makes less
explain: Liver synthesises albumin and clotting factors. Disease reduces synthesis.

q: In a flower, pollen lands on stigma, then pollen tube grows to ovule. What is the tube for?
opts: To carry sperm to egg for fertilisation
explain: Pollen tube delivers male gametes to ovule for fertilisation.

q: A student observes that a tadpole has gills and a frog has lungs. What does this show?
opts: Metamorphosis involves structural change for different habitat
explain: Metamorphosis adapts organism from aquatic to terrestrial life.

q: Why does a person with a blocked ureter have kidney pain?
opts: Urine backs up, increasing pressure in kidney
explain: Blockage prevents urine flow, pressure builds in kidney, pain and damage.

q: In a cross between two heterozygous plants (Aa x Aa), what is the ratio of dominant phenotype?
explain: 1 AA:2 Aa:1 aa gives 3 dominant:1 recessive phenotype.

q: A plant is grown in a dark room with a small hole for light. It bends towards hole. What is this?
explain: Shoot bends towards light, positive phototropism.

q: Why does a person with a cold have a runny nose?
opts: Mucus production increases to trap pathogens
explain: Inflammation increases mucus to trap and flush pathogens.

q: In an experiment, a student covers a leaf with Vaseline on both sides. It dies. Why?
opts: Vaseline blocks stomata, preventing gas exchange for photosynthesis and respiration
explain: Blocking stomata stops CO2 and O2 exchange, photosynthesis and respiration fail.

q: A person with blood group B has anti-A antibodies. What happens if given group A blood?
opts: Agglutination because anti-A attacks A antigens
explain: Anti-A antibodies bind A antigens, causing clumping and haemolysis.

q: In a food web, what is the role of decomposers?
opts: To break down dead matter and return nutrients
explain: Decomposers mineralise dead matter, releasing nutrients for producers.

q: Why does a seed with a hard coat not germinate until scarified?
opts: Hard coat prevents water and oxygen entry
explain: Impermeable coat blocks water and oxygen needed for germination. Scarification breaks it.

q: A student measures the rate of photosynthesis at different light intensities. Rate plateaus at high light. Why?
opts: Light is no longer limiting, CO2 or temperature limits
explain: At high light, another factor like CO2 becomes limiting, rate levels off.

q: In the eye, the iris controls pupil size. Why does pupil constrict in bright light?
opts: To reduce light entering and protect retina
explain: Pupil constriction limits light, preventing damage to retina.

q: A person with a diet low in iron develops anaemia. Why?
opts: Iron is needed for haemoglobin synthesis
Iron is needed for white cells
explain: Iron is component of haem. Without iron, less haemoglobin made.

q: In a population, a recessive allele causes disease only in homozygotes. Why does it persist?

q: Why does a plant with a tap root survive drought better than fibrous root?

opts: Energy is lost as heat, in respiration, excretion and egestion

q: A student observes that a butterfly has proboscis. What is its function?

explain: Without predators, herbivores rise, overgraze producers, producers fall.
